body.rationale: Governing IPS status: ratified per the run context, so the breaches the reviews cite are real. Faculty sign-off status was not stated beyond that. I put IPS-clean portfolios first, because the CIO needs something buildable. Four candidates have no hard breaches: resampled_efficient_frontier, cvar_minimization, inverse_volatility and black_litterman. All four rank in my top five. 1) resampled_efficient_frontier is clean on every limit and has the broadest diversification of the compliant return-based methods (effective N 13.1, backtest Sharpe 0.61). Averaging over resamples tames the estimation error that hurts max_sharpe. Its weakness is a thin drawdown margin, -24.84% against -25%, which Black-Litterman's reviewer flagged, so I would want it blended. 2) cvar_minimization is compliant and relies on tail and covariance structure, not return forecasts, which suits a late-cycle read. It has the best backtest drawdown of the compliant set (-18.7%) and a 0.74 backtest Sharpe. Its reviewers note that its 2.9 effective assets are concentrated and that its volatility is tuned to the 8% floor, so it ranks below the resampled portfolio. 3) inverse_volatility is compliant, has no tuned parameter, and is broadly spread (effective N 14.8). Its reviewers found only a minor imprecision, but it ignores correlation across a roughly 43% credit and sovereign cluster. 4) black_litterman is compliant, with a -21.9% drawdown and 0.68 backtest Sharpe. Its reviewers flagged a weak equilibrium prior from overlapping ETF AUM, which is why it sits fourth. 5) risk_parity is the best covariance-based, risk-structured option and has the lowest CRO risk score among the near-compliant ones (0.41). Its only breach is volatility, at 7.56% against the 8% floor. It beats the other family representatives on drawdown (-20.3%) and breadth (effective N 14.3). Reviewers did find that its effective-N claim measures capital dispersion rather than risk dispersion. The first choice beats the fifth because resampled_efficient_frontier meets every hard IPS limit with a higher ex-ante return (6.98% vs 6.43%), while risk_parity needs a blending partner to fix its volatility shortfall. The top five span four families: return_optimized, non_traditional, heuristic and risk_structured. I flag market_cap_weight. Its backtest drawdown is -40.6%, which is 15.6 points past the limit and is a floor given the 1993 sample start. Its CRO risk score is 0.80. The intra-category reviewer also showed that its weights are overlapping ETF AUM shares, not a true market portfolio, so the CAPM-efficiency premise does not hold. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier because its orthogonality is a feature in an ensemble, even though I do not rank it.
